documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV. 69F.

No new concerns. Walking her usual route most days, garden beds being turned over this week. No ED visits, no new medications, no falls.

HRA reviewed: fully independent in ADLs and IADLs. Lives alone, managing well. Vision and hearing adequate. PHQ-2 0.
Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert and conversational. Heart regular rate and rhythm. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Gait normal, no assistive device.

Plan:
- Osteopenia: DXA 6/2023 osteopenia with FRAX below threshold. Repeat late 2025. Diet and exercise as is.
- Annual labs today (CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c).
- Mammogram: 10/2023 negative; next one ordered for fall 2025.
- Vaccines up to date. Fall flu and COVID.
RTC one year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Carolyn - labs all fine. Blood sugar and A1c normal, cholesterol in a good range, kidney and liver tests normal, blood counts normal. Enjoy the garden.

documents.title: Vaccine Administration
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fall vaccines. Afebrile, feels well, no prior reactions. Fluzone High-Dose 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Moderna 2024-25 COVID 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. VIS provided. Observed 15 minutes, left in good condition.

documents.title: Breathing test from research study
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning. I signed up for a university study on how lungs change with age (they recruit healthy volunteers at the senior center). They did a breathing test last week and had me come back yesterday to repeat it. The numbers were lower than the young woman they compare everyone to and the ratio was lower too. I'm a little rattled. I've never smoked and I feel fine walking. Does this mean I'm getting lung disease? Do I need more tests or an inhaler? They said they'd send you a letter.

documents.title: RE: Breathing test from research study
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Carolyn, thanks for letting me know. Lung numbers are normally lower at 70 than at 20, so a comparison to a young adult by itself doesn't tell us much; what matters is how you compare with other women your age. No shortness of breath, cough or wheeze, and you are walking miles a day, which is reassuring. I'll read the full report as soon as it arrives and get back to you. No inhaler or extra testing for now.

reports.text: Research protocol spirometry, pre-bronchodilator. Three acceptable maneuvers, repeatable. Height 163 cm. FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC each above the lower limit of normal for age, sex and height (GLI reference). Values are lower than those of the protocol's healthy 20-year-old female reference. Flow-volume loop of normal configuration.
reports.conclusion: Spirometry within normal limits for age. No obstruction or restriction.

reports.text: Repeat research spirometry, one week after the first session, pre-bronchodilator. Good effort, acceptable and repeatable maneuvers. Results reproduce the 10/23/2024 session: FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC above the lower limit of normal for age, sex and height, and lower than the young-adult reference.

documents.title: Pulmonary Research Program Letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
University pulmonary and critical care research program
Re: Carolyn Sweeney, DOB 05/22/1954
Study visits 10/23/2024 and 10/30/2024

Dear Doctor,

Your patient enrolled as a healthy volunteer in our study of how lung function changes across the lifespan. One aim of the study is to describe FEV1 in older adults, since FEV1 is the measure most often used to predict pulmonary outcomes after surgery.

She reported being in excellent health, with no change in her exercise tolerance or stamina; she walks 2-3 miles daily and gardens. No shortness of breath, chest tightness, wheeze, cough, sputum or recent respiratory infection. No seasonal allergies or asthma. Sleeps flat without difficulty; no snoring, witnessed apneas or morning headaches. No prior lung disease and no respiratory hospitalizations. Never smoker, no secondhand smoke, no industrial or hazardous work exposure. Lives independently. No prescription medications. Allergies: no known drug allergies. No family history of lung disease. History of mild osteopenia.

Examination: vital signs normal, SpO2 98% on room air, BMI 22. Alert and cooperative. Lungs clear with normal vesicular breath sounds, no wheezes, rales or rhonchi. Heart regular without murmur or gallop. No clubbing or edema. Neurologic and musculoskeletal examinations normal.

Spirometry on 10/23 showed FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC lower than our healthy 20-year-old female reference; a repeat on 10/30 reproduced this. Against reference values for her own age, sex and height, every value is within normal limits. These differences are the expected effect of normal aging of the lungs and chest wall. Her FEV1 is well preserved for age.

She was surprised by the comparison and worried it meant early lung disease, and asked whether she needs more testing or treatment. We explained that it does not indicate lung disease and that no further testing or treatment is needed. We will see her for the one-year study follow-up.

Reports enclosed.

Pulmonary research fellow, for the study team

documents.title: Your research breathing tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Carolyn, the study team's letter came in and I've read both reports. Compared with women your age and height, all of your numbers are normal. The gap from the 20-year-old reference is just what happens to everyone's lungs over 50 years; it isn't disease. Your FEV1 (the main number) is in good shape for your age. Nothing to test or treat. Keep walking.

documents.title: RE: Your research breathing tests
documents.author: patient
documents.body: What a relief. They told me the same thing at the end but it helped to hear it from you. Thank you.

conditions.label: Age-related cognitive decline
conditions.note: Slower name and word recall, function intact, MoCA 26/30

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, 70F.

One thing she wanted to raise: she is slower than she used to be at pulling up names and the occasional word. A former student's name comes to her an hour later; she'll pause mid-sentence for a word. She keeps her calendar and pays her bills without trouble, hasn't missed appointments or medications (takes none), drives without getting lost, cooks, runs the house. No repeated questions per her own account. Mood good, sleeping well. No head injury, no new symptoms.

HRA: independent in all ADLs and IADLs. No falls. PHQ-2 0.
Meds: none. NKDA.
Interval: research lung testing 10/2024, normal for age.

Cognitive assessment: MoCA 26/30, within the normal range.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight up slightly. Alert, oriented, engaged, fluent speech. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema. Neuro: cranial nerves intact, strength and sensation normal, gait steady, no tremor.

A/P:
1. Age-related cognitive decline. Mild slowing of name and word retrieval with normal screening score and fully preserved function; consistent with normal aging, not MCI. B12 and TSH today. Discussed staying physically and socially active, reading, sleep. Repeat MoCA next year, sooner if she or anyone around her notices a change.
2. Osteopenia: DXA ordered for late 2025.
3. Annual labs: CMP, CBC, lipids.
4. Mammogram fall 2025, already ordered. Flu and COVID in the fall.
RTC 1 year.

orders.order: DXA bone density, hip and spine

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: B12 and thyroid are both normal, so nothing there is affecting your memory. The rest of your labs (blood count, kidneys, liver, cholesterol) are normal too. Plan stays as we talked about.

reports.text: Bilateral screening digital breast tomosynthesis. Comparison 10/18/2023 and 09/2021. Scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious masses, calcifications or distortion. Stable.

documents.title: Vaccine Administration
documents.author: MA
documents.body: High-dose flu R deltoid and 2025-26 Moderna COVID L deltoid. No contraindications on screening. Tolerated well. Pt mentioned her one-year research lung visit is in two weeks; told her we'll watch for the letter. Bone density reminder: DXA scheduled 11/17.

reports.text: Research protocol complete pulmonary function testing: spirometry, lung volumes by plethysmography and diffusing capacity. Acceptable and repeatable efforts. FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC, total lung capacity and DLCO all within normal limits for age, sex and height (GLI reference). All values lower than those of the study's healthy 20-year-old female control. No bronchodilator given per protocol.

documents.title: Pulmonary Research Program Follow-up Letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
University pulmonary and critical care research program
Re: Carolyn Sweeney, DOB 05/22/1954
One-year study visit 10/20/2025

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Sweeney returned for her one-year follow-up in our lung-aging study, this time for full lung function testing.

She feels well and remains very active, walking several miles a day and gardening. She denies dyspnea, chest pain, wheeze or chronic cough. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker. Family history: mother with osteoporosis, father with hypertension, a maternal aunt who fractured a hip at 78. Known mild osteopenia.

BMI 23. Lungs clear without wheezes, rales or rhonchi. Normal heart sounds. No peripheral edema.

For the study, her results are compared with those of a healthy 20-year-old woman tested in the same laboratory. Both are healthy and have no symptoms, yet their lung function differs considerably, as expected across five decades of normal aging. Measured against her own age, sex and height, her spirometry, lung volumes and diffusing capacity are all normal, and her FEV1 remains well preserved for age.

No clinical follow-up is needed from our standpoint. Thank you for allowing her participation.

Study physician, pulmonary research program
